title: Kilwa Sultanate founded
description: By tradition the Persian prince Ali ibn al-Hassan Shirazi founds the island city that comes to control the gold trade of the Swahili coast.

title: Kizimkazi Mosque
description: An inscription dates a mosque on Zanzibar, among the oldest Islamic buildings on the East African coast.

title: Ibn Battuta visits Kilwa
description: The Moroccan traveller describes Kilwa at the height of its wealth as one of the most beautiful and well-built cities he has seen.

title: Portuguese sack Kilwa
description: The fleet of Francisco de Almeida takes the city and builds a fort, and Kilwa's trade never recovers.

title: Omanis take Zanzibar
description: After driving the Portuguese from Mombasa the Omanis take control of Zanzibar and the coast.

title: Sultan Said moves his capital to Zanzibar
description: Said bin Sultan of Oman settles in Zanzibar, which grows rich on cloves, ivory and the slave trade.

title: Burton and Speke reach Lake Tanganyika
description: The two British explorers, following Arab caravan routes from the coast, are the first Europeans to see the lake.

title: Stanley meets Livingstone
description: The journalist Henry Morton Stanley finds the missing explorer David Livingstone on the shore of Lake Tanganyika.

title: Zanzibar slave market closed
description: Under British pressure Sultan Barghash signs a treaty ending the sea-borne slave trade and closing the market.

title: German East Africa chartered
description: The German government grants imperial protection to the lands for which Carl Peters had obtained treaties in the hinterland of Bagamoyo.

title: Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty
description: Germany recognises a British protectorate over Zanzibar in exchange for Heligoland, fixing the division of East Africa.

title: Battle of Lugalo
description: The Hehe under Chief Mkwawa destroy a German column, beginning seven years of resistance.

title: Anglo-Zanzibar War
description: British warships shell the palace of a sultan who had taken the throne without approval, and he flees within an hour.

title: Maji Maji Rebellion
description: Peoples of the south rise against forced cotton growing, and the German suppression and the famine that follows kill tens of thousands or more.

title: Battle of Tanga
description: A small German force under Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck beats off a British landing, the start of four years of fighting in East Africa.

title: British mandate over Tanganyika
description: The League of Nations confirms British rule over most of former German East Africa.

title: TANU founded
description: Julius Nyerere turns the Tanganyika African Association into a party demanding independence.

title: Independence of Tanganyika
description: Tanganyika becomes independent from Britain with Julius Nyerere as prime minister.

title: Zanzibar Revolution
description: A month after independence, African revolutionaries overthrow the sultan and the mainly Arab government, and thousands of Arabs and South Asians are killed.

title: Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
description: The two states unite in the republic soon renamed Tanzania.

title: Arusha Declaration
description: Nyerere sets out the policy of ujamaa, African socialism based on self-reliance, nationalisation and village farming.

title: TAZARA Railway completed
description: A Chinese-built line links the Zambian copperbelt to the port of Dar es Salaam, bypassing white-ruled southern Africa.

title: Nyerere steps down
description: Julius Nyerere retires after twenty-four years in power, and Ali Hassan Mwinyi begins to dismantle the socialist economy.

title: First multiparty election
description: Benjamin Mkapa of the ruling party wins the first contested election since the 1960s.

title: Sinking of the Bukoba
description: An overloaded ferry capsizes near Mwanza and several hundred people drown.

title: John Magufuli becomes president
description: The new president begins a campaign against corruption and waste alongside growing restrictions on opposition and the press.
